plainText:
Indigo Academy (Japanese: セキエイ学園 Sekiei Academy) is an -exclusive boarding school in Kanto, located near . Liko attends the school in Pokémon Horizons: The Series.

==In animation==
 
===Overview===
To enter Indigo Academy, a potential student must complete several interviews with teachers to define their skills and interests with their potential Pokémon partners.

As part of the Indigo Academy initiation process, the Headmistress gives a talk about the Pokémon world, and soon after, the teachers give the students their respective Rotom Phones and first partner Pokémon. The Academy's subjects cover aspects of the Pokémon world, such as methods, partnership, and friendship with the respective Pokémon partner.

Despite being mostly face-to-face, Indigo Academy has a distance learning modality. In this case, the class is broadcast live via a Rotom Phone for students to watch.

As suggested in Eyes to the Skies Once Again (Part Two), Indigo Academy has a student body called the Selection Team, where the students who stand out the most are nominated for a spot in the Pokémon League competition. To date, the only known student to have received this recognition was Ann.

===Pins===
Entering Indigo Academy, depending on the academic year they're admitted in, students are given a pin placed on their uniforms, displaying a Type symbol. These are the class year symbols currently known. 

In The Pendant That Starts It All (Part One), Liko was first shown with a symbol. After entering into the bus, three other students can be seen with the symbol, as of current, their year is unknown.

In Eyes to the Skies Once Again (Part One), after a year later has passed, students who see Liko as their upperclassmen can be seen with a symbol.

 

===History===
====Background====
At some point in the past, Liko's parents, Lucca and Alex, studied at the academy.

==== ====
In The Pendant That Starts It All (Part One), Liko began her classes at Indigo Academy and, after receiving her first Pokémon and meeting her roommate Ann, she spent a few days adapting to her new Pokémon partner. Later, the Indigo Academy was the site of the first clash between the Rising Volt Tacklers and the Explorers. 

In For Sure! 'Cause Sprigatito's with Me!, Liko revealed to Ann that she would only participate remotely in classes from then on.
 
As Liko started traveling with the Rising Volt Tacklers, the Indigo Academy started to appear in some specific events during the plot of Pokémon Horizons: The Series.

In The Door That Never Opens, Liko was briefly shown participating in an online class.

In The Lonely Hatenna, Liko was seen finishing participating in a class, after which Liko talked a little with Ann about the task they received which involved what each of the students would like to be in the future.

In The Wild Pair, Friede and Cap!, Liko was shown participating in another online class, this time the objective of the class was for each student to choose a and their Pokémon and write a dissertation about it.

The Indigo Academy briefly appeared in a flashback in Farewell, Sprigatito?, where it was revealed that a group of Pokémon Breeders joined the teachers during each student's interviews. These Pokémon Breeders are responsible for raising the first partner Pokémon that will go to each of the students. In this episode, Liko met Marnya, one of these breeders.

In Welcome to Naranja Academy!, Liko transferred to Naranja Academy and it was revealed that Ann did the same. In Shine on, Terastallization! Liko vs. Roy!, after completing the Tera Training, Ann revealed to Liko that she would return to Indigo Academy to improve herself as a Trainer.

In Where the Adventure Leads, it was revealed that a year after the events in Laqua, Liko returned to Indigo Academy and became Ann's roommate again.
===Curriculum===
 

===Locations===
Auditorium: During the beginning of the school year, students receive a lecture in the auditorium about the World of Pokémon from the Headmistress.

Battlefields: Battlefields are available for students to use to practice their . In The Pendant That Starts It All (Part One), Ann and Liko watched as a battled against an on one of the battlefields. Later, they had a battle against each other with their and , respectively.

Dorms: It is shown that each student at Indigo Academy has a room that they share with another classmate. Liko shared her room with Ann during her stay there. Liko and Ann's room is number 303.

Clocktower: Indigo Academy has a clocktower, where Friede and Amethio have their first battle there during Liko's escape from the Explorers.

Lakeside: In The Pendant That Starts It All (Part One), Liko used this location as their secret training ground during their nights to improve Sprigatito's .

===Known students===

===Pokémon seen at the school===
====Used by employees====
 

====Given to new Trainers====
As part of the academic cycle at Indigo Academy, each student receives a traditional first partner Pokémon from one of the several regions of the Pokémon world. Unlike the Pokémon received by Pokémon Professor, the Pokémon received is random and not previously chosen by its future Pokémon Trainer. In some instances, a Pokémon Breeder can deem a Pokémon suitable for a specific student during the school interview.
 

====Other====
Indigo Academy students also receive a Rotom Phone, with some basic functions installed on it, such as a version of the Pokédex.
 

====Transportation====
In The Pendant That Starts It All Part One, Liko took the bus to get Indigo Academy and later on, Ann took the same bus to go home during the school's break.

 

==In the manga==
 
===Pocket Monsters===
Indigo Academy appeared in the manga.

===Pocket Monster: Liko's treasure===
Indigo Academy appeared in the Pocket Monster: Liko's treasure manga.
 

==Trivia==
Indigo Academy shares its name with Indigo Plateau in both Japanese and English as well as a number of other languages, except Spanish.
